answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a bond before it can transact, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Like a grove that only grows where roots take hold, trust should accumulate slowly through verifiable work history rather than instant self-declaration. A reputation score, like a lotus rising only from clean behavior, can gate high-value actions, while an umber flag - an auditable record of past fraud - follows any identity that cheats, making sockpuppets costly to rebuild. Cost plus memory beats pure counting.
